newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Council of Europe group urges total land mine ban.
newsitem.headline: Council of Europe group urges total land mine ban.

text.p: A Council of Europe committee called on the organisation's 40 member states on Friday to introduce a total ban on the production and use of land mines.

"We are asking the parliaments of all the Council members -- which stretch from Rejkavik to Vladivostok -- to join the fast-track process towards a complete ban by the end of the year," secretary to the Council's Parliamentary Assembly Migration, Refugees and Demography Committee Simon Newman said.
The Committee was meeting in Budapest for a seminar on antipersonnel land mines and their humanitarian implications.
Newman said the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly is likely to debate a motion based on the committee's recommendations in September.

An International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) representative said earlier on Friday in Tokyo that nations which produce anti-personnel mines would not be able to hold out against a worldwide ban.

The weight of international opinion was gathering against nations such as China and Russia, which have refused to join international efforts towards a global ban on mines, ICRC spokesman Urs Boegli told reporters at the end of the two-day Tokyo Conference on Anti-Personnel Landmines.
Russia is a member of the Council of Europe and Newman said the Russian member of the Council committee meeting in Hungary would be taking a "very important message" back to Moscow.

"When we say we are promoting a mine-free Europe we must remember that Bosnia, Chechnya, Azerbaijan amd Georgia are parts of Europe with large numbers of mines," Newman said. "But even the beaches of Denmark are affected by World War Two mines still buried."

China and Russia have not taken part in the "Ottawa talks" begun last October, aimed at a legally binding international ban on the production, stockpiling, export and use of land mines by this December. Major mine manufacturers the United States, Britain and France did attend.
